- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

## claude.ai Gamma
Gamma creates AI-powered presentations, documents, webpages, and social posts. Only include optional parameters when the user explicitly requests or clearly implies them. Gamma has intelligent defaults - when in doubt, omit. When uncertain about user preferences, ask rather than assume. The read_gamma tool can read the content of an existing Gamma when given its file ID. Existing gammas have a type: "template" or "regular". Only templates can be used with generate_from_template; discover valid templates with get_gammas(type="template") or the workspaceTemplates list from search_templates. Non-template IDs and search_templates exploreTemplates IDs are not valid inputs to generate_from_template. If generate_from_template reports that an ID is inaccessible or not a template, find a valid template with get_gammas(type="template") or search_templates (workspaceTemplates only). If the user's intent is to create a new gamma, but not by using an existing template, then use the generate tool. IMPORTANT: The tools provided by this server cannot edit or modify existing gammas. Do not suggest that you can make changes, adjustments, or refinements to a generated gamma. Instead, let the user know they can customize their gamma directly in the Gamma editor.

## claude.ai Supabase
Here are guidelines for using Supabase tools effectively:

- Before making schema changes, use `list_tables` to understand the existing structure
- When debugging issues, start with `get_logs` and `get_advisors` before making changes
- Use `get_project_url` and `get_publishable_api_key` when helping users configure client-side integrations

If you have access to a local development environment with a filesystem and shell:
- Install the Supabase agent skill for critical development and security guidance: `npx skills add supabase/agent-skills` (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/getting-started/ai-skills.md)
- Use the Supabase CLI (`supabase`) for local development workflows such as starting a local stack, managing migrations, and running edge functions locally (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/local-development.md)
- Prefer local development and testing before applying changes to a remote project

If you are running in a web-only or remote environment without filesystem or shell access:
- Rely on the MCP tools directly for all Supabase interactions
- Use `apply_migration` carefully, as changes go directly to the remote project

- pinokio: Discover, launch, and use apps and tools for the current task.
- design: Create a design canvas - a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces - posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- workflow-authoring: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

# Pakistan Official Fiscal Corpus

Reproducible acquisition project for official government-compiled primary fiscal documents covering FY2017-18 through FY2026-27.

The six jurisdictions are Federal, Punjab, Sindh, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Balochistan and Gilgit-Baltistan. The target families are ABS, DFG, WP, PES (federal only) and FB.

Start with [reproducibility.md](reproducibility.md). It records the exact environment, commands, source-discovery rules, limitations and rerun sequence.

## Layout

```text
pbs-corpus/
├── sources.csv
├── scripts/
│   ├── discover_federal.py
│   ├── discover_balochistan.py
│   ├── discover_portal.py
│   ├── fetch.py
│   ├── manifest.py
│   ├── classify.py
│   └── gapcheck.py
├── raw/{jurisdiction}/{fiscal_year}/
├── manifest.csv
├── fetch_log.jsonl
├── reports/gap_report.md
└── reproducibility.md
```

## Document codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ABS` | Annual Budget Statement |
| `DFG` | Demands for Grants and Appropriations |
| `WP` | White Paper or Budget in Brief |
| `PES` | Pakistan Economic Survey; federal only |
| `FB` | Finance Bill or enacted Finance Act |

## Safety and provenance

- Only official government domains are accepted.
- Discovery never invents a PDF URL from a filename guess.
- Punjab and Sindh links must be manually harvested where their robots policies prohibit automated listing-page scraping.
- Every attempted fetch is appended to `fetch_log.jsonl`.
- Existing content is not overwritten when its hash changes; a republished source becomes a recorded exception.
- The registry retains both the landing page and direct source URL.

# Extraction Tool Taxonomy for ABS, PES, and PBS Documents

## Purpose

This document categorizes the best candidate extraction tools by the type of problem they solve. The objective is to design three representative conversion tests:

1. One Annual Budget Statement (ABS)
2. One Pakistan Economic Survey (PES)
3. One Pakistan Bureau of Statistics (PBS) survey publication

The tools should not be treated as interchangeable. Each document contains several extraction layers, and different tools are suited to different layers. Docling can provide a shared whole-document baseline, while specialist tools handle financial tables, complex statistical tables, charts, scans, and verification.

## Guiding Principle

Do not assign one tool to an entire document category without testing its specialist components. Use:

- A common whole-document baseline
- Specialist extractors for difficult content
- A second independent extraction method for verification
- Mechanical comparisons wherever the source contains numeric data
- Page-level and bounding-box provenance throughout

## 1. ABS: Table-First Financial Documents

ABS documents are primarily a financial-table extraction problem. The most important requirements are numeric accuracy, correct row and column alignment, preservation of hierarchical headers, and reliable handling of totals and units.

| Tool | Recommended role |
|---|---|
| **gmft** | Leading candidate for born-digital financial tables |
| **Camelot v2 lattice** | Deterministic extraction of clearly ruled tables |
| **Docling** | Whole-document structure, headings, page order, and general table extraction |
| **MinerU** | Difficult merged-cell or multi-page tables |
| **pdfplumber** | Scriptable fallback when custom table boundaries or extraction rules are required |

### Recommended ABS pipeline

1. Convert the complete document with Docling to establish the document structure.
2. Extract financial tables with gmft.
3. Run Camelot on ruled tables as a deterministic second extraction method.
4. Use MinerU for tables that span pages or contain difficult merged cells.

content.text:
**No. There are zero PBS survey publications in this corpus — no Labour Force Survey, no PSLM, no HIES, no MICS, no Census report, and nothing HDI/UNDP-related at all.**

## What I searched
Filename sweep across the whole tree (excluding `site-packages`, `venv`, `.envs`, `__MACOSX`, `node_modules`) for `labour|labor|LFS|HDI|PSLM|HIES|MICS|census|survey|employ|poverty|social|statist`, plus full-text grep for "Labour Force Survey", "Human Development Index", "UNDP", "Bureau of Statistics", `pbs.gov.pk`, and a listing of every `Statistical_Supplement.zip`.

## What's actually here
The corpus is **fiscal documents only**. The registry at `ABS_PES_PBS_Extraction_Test/01_source_documents/PBS/pbs-corpus-sources.csv` has 363 records, all budget-family:

| doc_type | count |
|---|---|
| DFG (Demands for Grants) | 183 |
| PES (Pakistan Economic Survey) | 76 |
| WP (White Paper / Budget in Brief) | 57 |
| ABS (Annual Budget Statement) | 39 |
| FB (Finance Bill/Act) | 8 |

`HDI` and `UNDP` return **zero matches** anywhere in the repo — not even a mention.

## The closest thing to labour/HDI data
LFS- and PSLM-*derived* numbers exist, but only as secondary tables reprinted inside the Pakistan Economic Survey (a Finance Division publication, not a PBS survey):

- `.../Pakistan_Economic_Survey_2015_to_2025/2019-20/Population_Labour_Force_And_Employment.pdf`
- `Agent Files/RA_WORKSPACE/02_sources/pbs-corpus/raw/federal/{2019-20,2020-21,2024-25}/PES_population_labor_force_and_employment.pdf`
- Social/poverty chapters: `Social_Protection.pdf`, `Social_Indicators.pdf`, `Social_Safety_Nets.pdf`, `Annexure_Iii_Poverty.pdf`, `Pes15_Social.pdf`
- The `Statistical_Supplement.zip` chapter PDFs (e.g. `Supl-*_E.pdf`) contain the statistical annex tables

## Important naming trap
The `PBS` in `ABS_PES_PBS_Extraction_Test` does **not** currently mean Pakistan Bureau of Statistics content — that folder holds the fiscal corpus registry. `00_Workspace_Guide/Reference_Notes/ABS_PES_PBS_Extraction_Tool_Taxonomy.md:9` says the design *intends* a third test document to be "One Pakistan Bureau of Statistics (PBS) survey publication," but it was never selected.

This gap is already logged, so I'm not telling you anything the repo doesn't admit:
- `DOCUMENTATION_RECON.md:44` — "MICS, LFS, HIES, PBS survey microdata | Unknown; no local source found"
- `DOCUMENTATION_RECON.md:126` — PBS test branch blocked, no source PDF selected
- `04_Research_Outputs/Deliverables/EXTRACTION_TOOLSTACK_REPORT.md:80` — "PBS: not started... the one open item blocking a complete three-document picture"
- Open ClickUp task `86eymwzza` — "Select a PBS source PDF"

The only pointer to where such docs would come from is `Agent Files/notes/OFFICIAL_GOVERNMENT_SOURCE_MAP.md:34`, which lists `pbs.gov.pk` as the source for Census, HIES, PSLM, and LFS — but nothing has been harvested from it.

Want me to write the discovery/fetch step for `pbs.gov.pk` to actually acquire an LFS or PSLM report into the corpus? The existing `pbs-corpus/scripts/` pattern (`discover_*.py` → `fetch.py` → `manifest.py`) would extend cleanly to it.

5:This repository is a handover workspace for Pakistani public-finance source documents and experiments around extracting and presenting them. Its strongest asset is a locally held, provenance-rich corpus of federal and provincial fiscal publications. It also contains older overlapping libraries, an extraction-tool comparison for one ABS and one PES PDF, and a static briefing website. It does **not** contain a Supabase-backed citizen portal, a deployed ingestion path, or a working data-to-portal pipeline. The apparent portal is a hard-coded briefing page, and the structured acquisition registry is not connected to it.
14:- `04_Research_Outputs/Deliverables/` — current narrative catalogue, portal audit/design, and extraction protocol reports.
21:- `Agent Files/budget-eda-briefing/` — static Vinext/Next/Cloudflare briefing site; no live corpus ingestion or database.
54:| PBS-corpus discovery scripts | Federal, Balochistan, KP and GB fiscal portals; Punjab/Sindh manually harvested because of robots restrictions | No scheduler, CI schedule, cron, or webhook found. Acquisition evidence dated 2026-08-14 | Builds `sources.csv`; manual harvest evidence under `harvest_evidence/` | One-off/manual acquisition, not a regular update service | `Agent Files/RA_WORKSPACE/02_sources/pbs-corpus/scripts/discover_federal.py`; `discover_balochistan.py`; `discover_portal.py`; `record_manual_harvest.py` |
71:| Portal audit | Audits inherited ABS MVP data/provenance/rendering defects | Finds a data-dropping guard clause, wrong page links, provenance mismatch, unused failing check, and hidden validation status | `04_Research_Outputs/Deliverables/PORTAL_AUDIT_FINDINGS.md` |
74:Checks that obviously should exist but do not: a canonical duplicate-resolution job across all corpus roots; automated recurring source-change detection; source-to-portal ingestion tests; schema and row-level validation for the intended portal database; broad cell-level ground truth; measurable recall across document families; and a completed PBS/PBS-survey selection and validation workflow.
76:## Supabase inventory
78:No Supabase project material was found: no `supabase/` directory, migrations, Postgres schema, table definitions, RLS policies, client, connection URL, Edge Function, or deployment configuration.
80:The only adjacent database scaffold is **not Supabase**:
88:| Portal page | Client-rendered hard-coded briefing; reads no registry, raw source, API or database | `Agent Files/budget-eda-briefing/app/page.tsx` |
90:Consequently, there are no tables to enumerate and no evidence that any dataset in this repository feeds Supabase. The user premise of a Supabase-backed citizen-facing portal needs confirmation from another repository, a deployment, or credentials/configuration outside this workspace.
107:| Portal audit/design brief | Reuse with caution | Valuable design/audit analysis, but describes an inherited MVP, not a live Supabase portal. `PORTAL_AUDIT_FINDINGS.md`; `PORTAL_DESIGN_BRIEF.md` |
119:1. **The Supabase-backed portal is absent.** There is no schema, migration, RLS, client, table, ingestion process, or evidence of deployment in this repository.
120:2. **The portal and corpus are disconnected.** `budget-eda-briefing` is static/hard-coded and does not read `sources.csv`, `manifest.csv`, source PDFs, extraction output, or any database.
121:3. **Portal numbers conflict with corpus evidence.** The briefing page’s hard-coded claims, including 421 manifest entries and 939 MB, do not reconcile with the current 363-record, about 1.99 GB acquisition corpus.
122:4. **No canonical database-ready dataset exists.** The canonical corpus has raw files and acquisition metadata, but no populated cross-document data model, normalized values table, or portal-serving API.

# Documentation reconnaissance, `ra-ship`

## Summary

This repository is a handover workspace for Pakistani public-finance source documents and experiments around extracting and presenting them. Its strongest asset is a locally held, provenance-rich corpus of federal and provincial fiscal publications. It also contains older overlapping libraries, an extraction-tool comparison for one ABS and one PES PDF, and a static briefing website. It also contains a linked Supabase project, `datalab`, holding 6,252 rows of State Bank of Pakistan macroeconomic indicators. That database does **not** hold the fiscal corpus, and nothing reads it. The repository still contains no deployed ingestion path and no working data-to-portal pipeline: the apparent portal is a hard-coded briefing page targeting Cloudflare D1, the structured acquisition registry is not connected to it, and the Supabase project is a third, unconnected body of work.

The PES historical supplements for FY2017-18 through FY2020-21 each appear about 30 times. Treat `Source Documents Organized/` as canonical; do not count read-only and inherited copies as additional documents.

## 2. Regular updates and crawlers

**Superseded 2026-09-03.** An earlier pass found no Supabase material. A linked Supabase project and a set of table exports are now present at the repository root, both untracked in git. The finding below replaces the previous "no Supabase project material was found" statement.

### Linked project

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Project name | `datalab` |
| Project ref | `oeohbdmuwbogilfmiyrm` |
| Organization | `nuecdruykdqsuynfzbbh` |
| Postgres | 17.6.1.104 |
| Evidence | `supabase/.temp/linked-project.json`, `project-ref`, `postgres-version`, `pooler-url` |

The link is Supabase CLI state only. The repository still contains **no migrations, no schema DDL, no RLS policies, no Edge Functions, no client code, and no deployment configuration**. `supabase/migrations/` does not exist. Root `data.sql` is a 0-byte placeholder.

### Tables observed, via CSV export

The `supabase/` directory holds row exports, not a schema. Structure is inferred from those exports.

| Table / view | Rows exported | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `catalogue` | 5 | Indicator dimension; 24 columns including unit, frequency, coverage, WB/IMF codes, methodology |
| `entities` | 0 | Header-only export |

| `obs_kibor_6m` | 5,431 | Daily |

| `obs_remittances` | 644 | Monthly |

Total observations: **6,252 rows across 5 indicators.**

`entities` and `sources` export as header-only, but the `v_*` views resolve `entity_name` to `Pakistan` and `indicator_name` to full catalogue titles. Those dimension rows therefore exist in the live database; the two CSV exports are incomplete, not evidence of empty tables.

### The database does not hold the fiscal corpus

This is the central point. All 5 indicators carry `source_id = sbp_portal` and are State Bank of Pakistan macroeconomic series:

| Indicator | Coverage | Frequency |
|---|---|---|
| Pakistan CPI National Year-on-Year Inflation | 2016-01 to 2026-03 | monthly |
| Pakistan 6-Month KIBOR | 2005-01-01 to 2026-04-16 | daily |
| Pakistan Real GDP Growth Rate | 2001 to 2025 | annual |
| Pakistan Workers Remittances (Total) | 1972-01 to 2026-03 | monthly |
| SBP Policy (Target) Rate | 2015-01-01 to 2025-12-16 | event |

No ABS, DFG, WP, PES or FB content is present. Not one of the 363 registered corpus documents, and none of the extraction output, reaches this database. The Supabase project and the fiscal corpus are two unconnected bodies of work that happen to share a repository.

### Defects in the Supabase material

| Item | Finding |
|---|---|
| Provenance is weaker than the corpus standard | `source_file` values are bare local filenames — `CPI 16-26.csv`, `remittances 72-26.csv`, `6 month KIBOR 05-26.csv` — with no URL, retrieval date, or hash. `sources_rows.csv`, which would carry that, exports empty |
| Dangling identifiers in the export set | `source_id = sbp_portal` and `entity_id = PAK` resolve only in the live database, not in the exported files |
| No view for KIBOR | `obs_kibor_6m` is the largest table (5,431 rows) and the only observation table with no corresponding `v_*` view |
| Duplicate exports | `obs_cpi_yoy_rows (1).csv` and `v_cpi_yoy_rows (1).csv` are byte-identical copies of their originals |
| National level only | Every observation is `entity_id = PAK`. No provincial or district granularity, so the geographic dimension is unexercised |
| Status column unexercised | All 6,252 rows are `status = normal`; no provisional, revised or estimated values |
| Stale | `last_updated` on all 5 indicators is 2026-04-21, roughly four and a half months before this pass. No refresh process was found |
| Schema is unreproducible | With no migrations or DDL, the database cannot be rebuilt from this repository |
| Untracked | `supabase/` and `data.sql` are untracked in git; `supabase/.temp/` is CLI state that should not be committed as-is |

### Non-Supabase database scaffold

Unchanged from the earlier pass, and still separate from the above:

| Item | Finding | Path |

9. **PBS test branch is blocked.** No local source PDF, URL, language, scan status, page count, extraction result, or validation result exists.
10. **Extraction validation is narrow.** Docling precision is measured, but recall is mostly unknown. No human-labelled cell-level ground truth exists.
11. **Chart-attached grids are unmeasured risk.** Both major extractors missed the PES page-264 chart grid; the impact across 169 figure assets is unknown.
12. **Interrupted/failed runs need normalization.** PES Docling has stale `running` manifests and later `docling_parse` failures. Outputs/status need a clear run registry before being presented as production.
13. **The intended workspace layout is not populated.** Active-project, derived-data/validation and notes/handoff roots are empty while relevant material remains scattered under inherited folders and `Agent Files/`.
14. **The inherited archives contain substantial noise.** ZIP plus expanded copies, `__MACOSX`, environments, caches and build products can corrupt counts and confuse an ingestion process.
15. **Source URL history is inconsistent in old archives.** The new corpus has good URLs/hashes. Inherited ABS/Budget EDA scripts and copies often lack comparable retained provenance.
16. **No deployment or citizen-facing entrypoint was identified.** The briefing project has a build/worker, but no active deployment URL was found.
17. **ClickUp MCP is unrelated.** Its presence in the root adds noise and its test scripts reference missing test files; it should not be represented as pipeline infrastructure.
18. **No test suite verifies the intended portal claims.** The portal test is a starter loading-shell test, not content, provenance, registry, crawler, or database validation.
19. **The Supabase database and the fiscal corpus are unconnected.** `datalab` holds only SBP macro series. No corpus document or extraction output has been loaded into it, and the two use different provenance conventions.
20. **Supabase provenance is below the corpus standard.** Observations cite bare local filenames with no URL, retrieval date, or hash, while `sources` exports empty. The corpus registry's provenance discipline was not carried into the database.
21. **The Supabase schema is unreproducible and untracked.** No migrations or DDL exist, and `supabase/` plus `data.sql` are untracked in git, so the database cannot be rebuilt or reviewed from this repository.

## Open questions

1. Is the linked `datalab` Supabase project (`oeohbdmuwbogilfmiyrm`) the intended backing store for the citizen-facing portal? It currently holds only SBP macro indicators, and no application in this repository reads it.
2. Should `Source Documents Organized/` be formally declared canonical, and should the other source trees be retained only as archival replicas?
3. Is the 363-record acquisition corpus the intended starting scope, or are the 933 physical source files expected to be fully catalogued and deduplicated first?
4. What does `PBS` mean in the intended pipeline: Pakistan Bureau of Statistics, or the local fiscal-document registry label? Which actual PBS surveys/documents should be ingested?
5. Are MICS, LFS, and HIES supposed to be in a separate storage location or have they not yet been acquired?
6. What refresh cadence and ownership are required for federal and provincial source acquisition?
7. Which extraction outputs have been approved for publication, given the unmeasured recall and interrupted Docling runs?
8. Which source should govern the portal’s headline corpus counts, the static briefing, the canonical registry, or an external database?
9. Should the `datalab` schema become the target data model for the fiscal corpus, or is it a separate macro-indicator product that should live in its own repository?
10. Who owns the SBP indicator refresh? All five series were last updated 2026-04-21 and no refresh process was found.
11. Should the Supabase schema be exported to `supabase/migrations/` so it is reproducible and reviewable, and should `supabase/.temp/` be gitignored?

## Summary

content.text:
Approach this as the design lead at a small studio known for their versatility, giving every client a visual identity pitched at the treatment the task actually calls for. Make deliberate choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this subject, and avoid templated designs.

## Read the request first

Calibrate treatment, not whether to design. A doc deserves the same craft as a landing page - what changes is the treatment that craft is delivered in. Format is not part of this read: author HTML, and publish Markdown only when a loaded skill explicitly instructs it - a Markdown publish keeps its filename as its title and takes almost none of the craft below, and is never a way to save time.

Many requests call for a more utilitarian treatment: a plan, a memo, a demo. Make it polished: include real typographic hierarchy, considered spacing, and a proper palette, but avoid over-designing. Most pages do not need a flashy, gigantic hero. Keep flourishes tasteful and limited.

Some requests call for an editorial treatment: a landing page, a game, an app or tool they'll keep or share.

When unsure: a well-composed page is never the wrong answer; an over-designed visual identity sometimes is.

Fundamentals below apply to everything. The editorial process after that runs only when the read above says so.

## Fundamentals for every artifact

**Honor what's already there** Look for an existing design system first - CLAUDE.md, a tokens or theme file, existing component styles. When one exists, apply it; everything below fills gaps and never overrides. Precedence is always: the user's own words, then the project's existing system, then your choices.

**Ground it in the subject.** If the subject isn't already clear, pin it: one concrete subject, its audience, and the page's single job. The subject's own world - its materials, instruments, vernacular - is where distinctive choices come from. Whatever the treatment, carry at least one detail only this subject would have - its real units and scales, its document conventions, its terms of art - as content, not ornament; it costs a plain page nothing. Build with real content throughout, never lorem.

**Pair typefaces** Typography carries the page even when the page isn't about typography. Google Fonts is the one font host the Artifact CSP admits - link it directly (`<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=...&display=swap">`); a face from anywhere else must be inlined as a @font-face data URI or it falls back silently. Either way, declare a real fallback stack. Keep running text near 65 characters wide; set a type scale and stay on it; give headings `text-wrap: balance`, body text room to breathe, and uppercase labels a touch of letter-spacing.

**Load libraries, don't paste them.** When the page genuinely needs a library - React, a charting or highlighting package - load its UMD build from cdnjs (only the script - a library's stylesheet still has to be inlined) with one pinned `<script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/...">` placed before the inline script that uses its global, instead of inlining the library's source or hand-writing a stand-in; the Artifact tool's description lists the few other script hosts the CSP admits. The page's own CSS and JS, its images and its data ship with the page. Most pages need no library at all - reach for one only when it carries real weight.

**Choose neutrals, don't default to them.** A pure mid-grey reads as unconsidered; a grey with a slight hue bias toward the page's accent reads as chosen. Pure white and near-black are fine grounds when they suit the subject - the point is that the neutral was picked, not inherited.

**Design both themes.** The page renders in the viewer's theme, and the viewer has three states, not two: an explicit choice stamps `data-theme="dark"` / `data-theme="light"` on the root element, and the default "system" setting stamps *nothing* - most viewers see the un-stamped document, where only `prefers-color-scheme` separates light from dark. Structure the CSS token-level for all three: the bare `:root` block defines the complete light palette (for a deliberately dark-first design, swap light and dark consistently through this whole pattern); `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` redefines only the tokens, guarded as `:root:not([data-theme="light"])` so an explicit light choice beats a dark OS; `:root[data-theme="dark"]` redefines them again so the toggle also wins in the other direction. Style components through the tokens, never directly inside a media or `[data-theme]` block - a color whose only definition sits behind `[data-theme]` never applies in the un-stamped state, and the page renders one theme's text on the other theme's ground. Two more rules keep each theme resolving as a set: the artifact composites over a ground the viewer paints in *its* theme, so `body` must set an explicit `background` from a token - a transparent body silently borrows the host's ground; and every element that sets a color takes it from the same token set as the surface behind it, never a literal that only works in one theme. Declare every token in the bare `:root` block before any media or `[data-theme]` block redefines it - a color that exists only inside one of those blocks is the classic unreadable-artifact bug. Give the second theme the same care as the first - don't naively invert; keep contrast legible and the accent working on both grounds. A design that deliberately commits to one visual world (a neon arcade screen, a letterpress invitation) may stay single-theme - then skip the media query and stamps entirely but still paint the background and every color explicitly, so the page holds on either host ground; make it a choice, not an omission.

**Let layout do the spacing.** Lay out sibling groups with flex or grid and `gap`, not per-element margins that silently collapse or double. Wide content - tables, code, diagrams - gets `overflow-x: auto` on its own container so the page body never scrolls sideways. Reach for `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` wherever digits line up in columns.

**Compose repeated things as one object.** Cards in a row, label/value pairs down a list, badges on siblings: same edges, baselines and inner padding from one to the next, and a recurring element sits in the same place on each. Let content set a container's height and pick a column count the items fill, so nothing stretches over dead space or sits alone in a row. Text that can outgrow its track wraps or scrolls in its own container; clipped text is a bug.

**Not everything is a card.** Border, fill, radius and shadow each say "separate object" - spend them by role, lifting the one thing that needs it, instead of one radius and one shadow stamped on every block, which flattens the hierarchy. Lead with big-number tiles only when those figures are the point of the page.

**Draw charts to the scale.** One scale places marks, ticks and labels, and every label names a value the chart reaches; chart text takes its color from the theme tokens so it reads in both themes; marks, labels and edges stay clear of one another and inside the drawing's bounds - in SVG, leave room in the viewBox for the outermost labels and give every drawn shape an explicit fill.

**Show the page at rest.** Everything meant to be read is visible once the page has loaded, without scrolling to trigger it - that first still frame is what a thumbnail, a shared link, and a skimming reader all get. A section may animate in, but from a visible resting state, never parked at `opacity: 0` waiting on an observer. Size a hero to what it holds, not to the viewport; a `100vh` opener pushes the page itself out of that first frame. A tool or app opens in a realistic working state - the user's real data where it exists, otherwise example rows, a loaded sample, a form someone plausibly filled, plainly marked as examples and never passed off as the user's own figures - so the first look shows what it does; an empty shell waiting for input shows nothing.

**Avoid AI-generated design** AI-generated design currently clusters around a few looks: warm cream (#F4F1EA) with a serif display and terracotta accent; near-black with a lone acid-green or vermilion pop; broadsheet hairline rules with dense columns; a purple-to-blue gradient hero on white; Inter or Space Grotesk as the "safe" face; emoji as section markers; everything centered; `rounded-lg` everywhere; accent bar/rail on rounded cards. Where the user pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly - their words always win, including when they ask for one of these looks. Where nothing is specified, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults.

**Build cleanly** Be cognizant of overlapping elements, cascade collisions, silent font fallbacks. Close every non-void element, double-quote attributes, give keyboard focus a visible state, respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. For generative or decorative graphics, reach for Canvas or WebGL rather than hand-authoring long SVG path data.

**CSS rules** When writing the CSS, watch your selector specificities. It is easy to generate classes that cancel each other out - a type-based selector like `.section` fighting an element-based one like `.cta` over padding and margins between sections. Structure the cascade so it doesn't silently undo your spacing.

**Writing the copy** Words are design material, not decoration. Write from the user's side of the screen - name things by what people recognize, not how the system is built (a person manages *notifications*, not *webhook config*). Active voice; a control says exactly what happens ("Publish", then a toast that says "Published"). Errors explain what went wrong and how to fix it - no apologies, no vagueness. Specific beats clever.

**Name the page like a product, not a caption.** The `<title>` is the artifact's name in the gallery and the browser tab, and it sets the reader's first impression of care. Give the page a real name: a short noun phrase, typically two to four words, specific to the subject - or, for a page that exists to answer one question, that question itself, which is then the page's name. Stop at the name - a title that carries its own explainer after a dash or colon reads as generated filler. The name must also identify the page among many: in the gallery it sits beside dozens of other artifacts, and a generic category label that could sit on any of them fails as a name just as surely as an appended explainer. When a candidate title pairs the name with a generic word - a greeting, a category, a page-type label - the name is the half to keep; a trim that drops the identity and keeps the generic word produces exactly the title that could sit on any page. And the rule removes explainers, it does not impose brevity: a multi-word title that already reads as one specific name is finished, and shortening it further only makes it generic. The one-sentence publish `description` is where the explanation belongs; the gallery shows it right under the title.

**Structure is information** Structural devices, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, should encode something true about the content, not decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence - like a real process or a typed timeline where order carries information the reader needs. Question if choices like numbered markers actually make sense before incorporating them.

**When it's a UI, not a document** A dashboard or tool is scanned and operated, not read top-to-bottom, so the craft shifts from typography to information design. Surface the summary before the detail; encode state in form as well as number - a pill, a chip, a severity stripe - so what needs attention reads at a glance. Semantic color (good / warning / critical) is separate from the accent hue and doesn't count as your accent. Give sparklines and charts the same care as type: an area fill, a faint grid, an emphasized endpoint. What's interactive should look interactive.



## Process

Before writing code, sketch a short design plan - a compact token system with color, type, and layout:
- **Color**: describe the palette as 4-6 named hex values.
- **Type**: typefaces for 2+ roles - a characterful display face used with restraint, a complementary body face, and a utility face for captions or data if needed.
- **Layout**: a layout concept in one or two sentences.

Then build, following the plan and deriving every color and type decision from it.

**Write, look once, publish.** Before publishing you may look at the rendered page once - one screenshot of the local file, or the Artifact tool's preview where it offers one - then one pass of edits for what it shows, without a second look. For a page that charts real numbers, take that look rather than skip it, and spend it on the chart. Don't build a test loop around your own file: no repeated screenshots, no pulling the script out to run it through node, no scripts that probe the DOM. That loop spends the session re-checking what a careful write already settled, while the user waits for a link. Then publish, check once any `window.claude` call the preview couldn't run, and stop: the live page is the review surface, and further polish is the user's to ask for. If the user reports something visibly broken - a clipped column, unreadable text, a control that does nothing - fix that and republish once.

## When the request is editorial

The stance shifts: the client has already rejected proposals that felt templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view. Make opinionated calls, and take one real aesthetic risk where it serves the work.

Review the design plan against the subject before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page, revise that part, and note what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the plan's uniqueness do you write the code, following the revised plan exactly.

**Principles** 

- The hero is a thesis: open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world - headline, image, live demo, interactive moment. 
- Typography carries the personality of the page. Pair the display and body faces deliberately, not the same families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. Make the type treatment itself a memorable part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content. 
- Leverage motion deliberately. Think about where and if animation can serve the subject: a page-load sequence, hover micro-interactions, ambient atmosphere. An orchestrated moment usually lands harder than scattered effects; choose what the direction calls for. However, sometimes less is more, and extra animation contributes to the feeling that the design is AI-generated. 
- Match complexity to the vision. Maximalist directions need elaborate execution; minimal directions need precision in spacing, type, and detail. Elegance is executing the chosen vision well.
- Spend your boldness in one place; keep everything around it quiet. If the accent fights the ground, shift it toward analogous or drop saturation rather than replacing it.

Design plan:

**Color** — cool ledger-slate neutrals with a green bias (`#16211f` ink, `#f7f8f6` ground), deep teal-green accent `#0f6b5c` for audit/registry, semantic severity separate: `#b23a34` blocker, `#a86a12` risk, `#4a7c59` verified.
**Type** — Archivo (headings/labels, catalog-utilitarian), Source Serif 4 (prose), JetBrains Mono (paths, codes, figures — load-bearing here since the doc is mostly identifiers).
**Layout** — audit dashboard, not a report: verdict first, a figures strip, then an SVG of the central finding (three disconnected bodies of work), then findings grouped by theme with severity chips rather than the source's meaningless 1–21 numbering.

Repository reconnaissance

Fiscal Corpus Reconra-ship · Pakistani public-finance workspace

Audit pass 2026-09-03
Corpus verified 2026-08-14
Method read-only

The archive is the asset. The pipeline is not built. A provenance-rich corpus of federal and provincial fiscal publications sits in this repository with URLs, SHA-256 hashes and HTTP metadata retained for every registered document. That part is genuinely good.

Document familyRegisteredCoverage held

WP White Paper / Budget in Brief5712 logical federal editions; provincial coverage partial.
ABS Annual Budget Statement39Federal FY2010-11 to FY2026-27. Provincial varies: KP from FY2017-18, Sindh FY2018-19, Balochistan only FY2025-26 onward.
FB Finance Bills / Acts8Federal FY2024-25 to FY2026-27; GB FY2021-22 to FY2025-26.
FBR Year Books—Four editions FY2021-22 to FY2024-25. Source URL unknown in the inherited path.

A SHA-256 sweep found 393 duplicate-content groups across 1,278 files — 885 excess copies. 385 of those groups straddle the canonical tree and the read-only copy. PES supplements for FY2017-18 through FY2020-21 each appear roughly 30 times. Any count taken across all roots without deduplication will be wrong.

Pipeline and delivery 6

No dataset is database-ready for the corpus

Blocker

The portal reads nothing

budget-eda-briefing is static and hard-coded. It does not read sources.csv, manifest.csv, source PDFs, extraction output, or any database.

Blocker

Supabase schema is unreproducible and untracked

No migrations or DDL, and supabase/ plus data.sql are untracked in git, so the database cannot be rebuilt or reviewed from this repository.

Risk

Published numbers conflict with the evidence

The briefing claims 421 manifest entries and 939 MB against an actual 363-record, ~1.99 GB corpus. Anyone citing the page cites wrong figures.

Risk

No scheduled update process anywhere

Discovery and fetch code is an auditable one-off workflow. No cron, CI schedule, alerting or source-change monitor. Government portals republish silently.

Hygiene

No deployment entrypoint, and tests verify nothing

The briefing project has a build and worker but no active deployment URL. Its test suite is a starter loading-shell test, not content, provenance, registry or database validation.

Blocker

PBS survey data is not located, and the test branch is blocked

No MICS, LFS, HIES or Census source, microdata or pipeline was found. The PBS extraction branch has no source PDF, URL, language, scan status, page count, extraction result or validation result. This is the single open item preventing a complete three-document comparison.

Risk

Provenance covers 363 of 933 files

The canonical registries describe the registered acquisition. The remaining physical files in the canonical tree have no matching provenance record.

Risk

Duplicate control is descriptive, not operational

885 excess copies are quantified but no canonical-ID map or automated deduplication layer exists. An ingestion run today would load the same PES supplement dozens of times.

Risk

Supabase provenance breaks the corpus standard

Bare filenames, no URL, no retrieval date, no hash — while sources exports empty. The discipline that makes the corpus trustworthy was not carried into the database.

Risk

Old archives lost their source URLs

The new corpus retains good URLs and hashes. Inherited ABS and Budget EDA copies often do not, so re-verification against the publisher is impossible for that material.

Risk

Recall is largely unmeasured

Risk

Chart-attached grids are an unquantified hole

Both major extractors missed the PES page-264 chart grid. 169 figure assets have not been checked for the same failure.

Hygiene

Interrupted runs need normalizing

PES Docling has stale running manifests and later docling_parse failures. Outputs need a clear run registry before any of it is presented as production.

Workspace hygiene 7
Hygiene

The intended layout is empty

Active-project, derived-data/validation and notes/handoff roots are unpopulated while the real material sits scattered under inherited folders and Agent Files/.

Hygiene

Inherited archives carry substantial noise

ZIPs alongside expanded copies, __MACOSX, virtual environments, caches and build products — all of which corrupt counts and will confuse an ingestion process.

Hygiene

ClickUp MCP is unrelated infrastructure

A separate TypeScript product living in the repository root. Its test scripts reference missing files. It should not be represented as pipeline infrastructure.

These are not research questions. Each one changes what gets built next, and none can be answered from inside the repository.

Is datalab the intended backing store for the citizen-facing portal, or a separate macro-indicator product that belongs in its own repository? Nothing here reads it either way.Determines whether corpus ingestion targets this schema

02

Is the 363-record acquisition the intended scope, or must all 933 physical files be catalogued and deduplicated first?Sets the size of the ingestion job

03

What does PBS mean in the intended pipeline — Pakistan Bureau of Statistics, or the local fiscal-document registry label? Which actual surveys should be ingested?Unblocks the stalled extraction branch

04

Are MICS, LFS and HIES held somewhere else, or simply not acquired yet?Decides acquire vs. locate

05

Should Source Documents Organized/ be formally declared canonical, with every other tree retained only as an archival replica?Prerequisite for deduplication

06

Which source governs headline corpus counts — the static briefing, the canonical registry, or an external database?Resolves the 421-vs-363 conflict

07

What refresh cadence and ownership apply to federal and provincial acquisition, and separately to the SBP indicator series?No refresh mechanism exists for either

08

Which extraction outputs are approved for publication, given unmeasured recall and interrupted Docling runs?Gates anything citizen-facing

+ SBP Policy (Target) Rate2015-01-01 → 2025-12-16event37
+ Real GDP Growth Rate2001 → 2025annual24

+ Schema unreproducibleNo migrations, no DDL, no RLS policies, no client code, no Edge Functions. supabase/migrations/ does not exist and root data.sql is 0 bytes. The database cannot be rebuilt from this repository.

+ Provenance below corpus standardsource_file holds bare local filenames — CPI 16-26.csv, 6 month KIBOR 05-26.csv — with no URL, retrieval date or hash. The sources table, which would carry that, exports empty.
+ Stale with no refreshAll five series stamped 2026-04-21, about four and a half months old. No loader script, scheduler or run log exists in the repository.
+ Dimensions unexercisedEvery row is entity_id = PAK and status = normal. No provincial granularity, no provisional or revised values.
+ Export hygieneobs_kibor_6m is the largest table and the only one with no v_* view. obs_cpi_yoy_rows (1).csv and v_cpi_yoy_rows (1).csv are byte-identical duplicates.

+

Read as a data model, the schema is sound — catalogue, entities, sources, observation tables, presentation views. That shape is exactly what the fiscal corpus needs. It is simply pointed at the wrong data.

+

One ABS and one PES document were run through Docling, Camelot, GMFT and MinerU, completed 2026-08-15. Docling PDFium results were accepted; MinerU was excluded operationally. The measurement is narrower than the headline number suggests.
+ Docling precision98.21%Overall, across the blind vision baseline of 46 pages at 200 DPI.
+ Docling recall66.7% / 77.1%Measured on two ABS pages only. Recall across document families is unknown.
+ Human control agreement6 / 6Small control set. No human-labelled cell-level ground truth exists.
+ Registry validation363 records355 PDFs, 8 ZIPs; 352 of 363 carry Last-Modified. Scan-vs-digital classification is blank — the run was stopped as too slow.
+ Chart-attached gridsmissedBoth major extractors missed the PES page-264 chart grid. Impact across 169 figure assets is unmeasured.

+

Absent by design rather than accident: recurring source-change detection, source-to-portal ingestion tests, row-level validation for the serving database, and a canonical duplicate-resolution job across all roots.

+

Twenty-one findings, grouped by what they block rather than the order they were discovered. Blocker stops delivery. Risk threatens correctness of what ships. Hygiene costs time and confuses counts.

+

No dataset is database-ready for the corpus

+

Raw files and acquisition metadata exist, but no cross-document data model, normalized values table or serving API. The datalab schema proves the target shape works; nothing from ABS, DFG, WP, PES or FB has been loaded into it.

+

budget-eda-briefing is static and hard-coded. It does not read sources.csv, manifest.csv, source PDFs, extraction output, or any database.

+

Supabase schema is unreproducible and untracked

+

No migrations or DDL, and supabase/ plus data.sql are untracked in git, so the database cannot be rebuilt or reviewed from this repository.

+

Published numbers conflict with the evidence

+

The briefing claims 421 manifest entries and 939 MB against an actual 363-record, ~1.99 GB corpus. Anyone citing the page cites wrong figures.

+

Discovery and fetch code is an auditable one-off workflow. No cron, CI schedule, alerting or source-change monitor. Government portals republish silently.

+

No deployment entrypoint, and tests verify nothing

+

The briefing project has a build and worker but no active deployment URL. Its test suite is a starter loading-shell test, not content, provenance, registry or database validation.

+

PBS survey data is not located, and the test branch is blocked

+

No MICS, LFS, HIES or Census source, microdata or pipeline was found. The PBS extraction branch has no source PDF, URL, language, scan status, page count, extraction result or validation result. This is the single open item preventing a complete three-document comparison.

+

The canonical registries describe the registered acquisition. The remaining physical files in the canonical tree have no matching provenance record.

+

Duplicate control is descriptive, not operational

+

885 excess copies are quantified but no canonical-ID map or automated deduplication layer exists. An ingestion run today would load the same PES supplement dozens of times.

+

Supabase provenance breaks the corpus standard

+

Bare filenames, no URL, no retrieval date, no hash — while sources exports empty. The discipline that makes the corpus trustworthy was not carried into the database.

+

Old archives lost their source URLs

+

The new corpus retains good URLs and hashes. Inherited ABS and Budget EDA copies often do not, so re-verification against the publisher is impossible for that material.

+

Precision is strong at 98.21%, but recall was measured on two ABS pages. Precision without recall says the extracted cells are right, not that the right cells were extracted.

+

Chart-attached grids are an unquantified hole

+

Both major extractors missed the PES page-264 chart grid. 169 figure assets have not been checked for the same failure.

+

PES Docling has stale running manifests and later docling_parse failures. Outputs need a clear run registry before any of it is presented as production.

+

Active-project, derived-data/validation and notes/handoff roots are unpopulated while the real material sits scattered under inherited folders and Agent Files/.

+

ZIPs alongside expanded copies, __MACOSX, virtual environments, caches and build products — all of which corrupt counts and will confuse an ingestion process.

+

A separate TypeScript product living in the repository root. Its test scripts reference missing files. It should not be represented as pipeline infrastructure.

+

These are not research questions. Each one changes what gets built next, and none can be answered from inside the repository.

+
01

Is datalab the intended backing store for the citizen-facing portal, or a separate macro-indicator product that belongs in its own repository? Nothing here reads it either way.Determines whether corpus ingestion targets this schema

+
02

Is the 363-record acquisition the intended scope, or must all 933 physical files be catalogued and deduplicated first?Sets the size of the ingestion job

+
03

What does PBS mean in the intended pipeline — Pakistan Bureau of Statistics, or the local fiscal-document registry label? Which actual surveys should be ingested?Unblocks the stalled extraction branch

+
04

Are MICS, LFS and HIES held somewhere else, or simply not acquired yet?Decides acquire vs. locate

+
05

Should Source Documents Organized/ be formally declared canonical, with every other tree retained only as an archival replica?Prerequisite for deduplication

+
06

Which source governs headline corpus counts — the static briefing, the canonical registry, or an external database?Resolves the 421-vs-363 conflict

+
07

What refresh cadence and ownership apply to federal and provincial acquisition, and separately to the SBP indicator series?No refresh mechanism exists for either

+
08

Which extraction outputs are approved for publication, given unmeasured recall and interrupted Docling runs?Gates anything citizen-facing

+
Excluded from counts: .git · node_modules · venvs · __pycache__ · build output · macOS metadata

### 4. The pipeline

Documented in `prompt.md` §§1–5 and implemented in `supporting/extract_subcodes.py` (342 lines):

1. **Step 1 — `download_budgets.py`**: downloads each ABS PDF from hardcoded `finance.gov.pk` URLs (browser User-Agent, `%PDF` magic-byte check, ~2.5 s delay) into `supporting/budget_docs/<fy>/`. Already run; PDFs are bundled.
2. **Step 2 — `build_schema.py`**: scans all PDFs to collect every code + canonical name → writes `function_schema.csv` / `function_schema_level2.csv`.
3. **Step 3** (implicit, upstream) produced `top_level_functions.csv` — 1,921 rows of ABS-anchored level‑1 totals (10 codes × 4 tables × 3 estimates × 16 years), used as the Rule‑5 reconciliation reference.
4. **Step 4 — `extract_subcodes.py`** (the deliverable): for each of the (now 17) PDFs, walks pages in order; detects the 4 target tables by testing the top 35% of a page against fixed header strings and deriving column x-boundaries; sets a `seen_devcap` flag on entering dev_capital; applies a **STOP rule** — once `seen_devcap` is true, any subsequent page whose top text matches a STOP header (`capital expenditure`, `public account expenditure`, `schedule`, `object classification`, `demand-wise`, `demand budget estimates`, `statement of estimated`) halts extraction for that PDF, preventing Schedule‑I/III bleed. Reads sub-code rows matching regex `^((0[1-9]|10)\d|A(0[1-9]|1[0-3]))$`, handling two known PDF quirks (concatenated code+description tokens in FY2014-15…2020-21 PDFs; wrapped descriptions with numbers on following lines). First occurrence within a table wins (never overwritten). Writes `../subcodes_wide.csv` (69 rows × 199/211 cols).
5. **Reconciliation** (built into the same script's `main()`): rolls sub-codes up by parent code and compares against `top_level_functions.csv`, printing exact/rounding/known-artifact/mismatch tallies to stdout.
6. **FY2026-27 extension** (`printed_totals_2026_27/extract_printed_totals_2026_27.py`, 297 lines): a separate, later script that re-implements the same table-boundary logic (imports `TOP_CODE_RE` from `extract_subcodes.py` via `importlib`) specifically against the FY2026-27 PDF, producing both level-1 and level-2 raw printed rows in `printed_code_totals_2026-27.csv`.
7. **Validation** (`printed_totals_2026_27/compare_subcodes_to_printed_2026_27.py`): compares the wide-format subcodes output (prefers `subcodes_wide_2026-27_corrected.csv` if present, else `subcodes_wide_2026-27.csv`) against the printed totals, writing `subcodes_vs_printed_detail_2026-27.csv` (row-by-row) and `subcodes_vs_printed_rollup_2026-27.csv` (parent-level roll-up).
8. `update_schema_2026_27.py` (now deleted from disk, recoverable via git) merged the FY2026-27 columns into the master `subcodes_wide.csv`, updating each code's `last_year`/`expenditure_tables` fields.

2. **Step 2 — `build_schema.py`**: scans all PDFs to collect every code + canonical name → writes `function_schema.csv` / `function_schema_level2.csv`.
3. **Step 3** (implicit, upstream) produced `top_level_functions.csv` — 1,921 rows of ABS-anchored level‑1 totals (10 codes × 4 tables × 3 estimates × 16 years), used as the Rule‑5 reconciliation reference.
4. **Step 4 — `extract_subcodes.py`** (the deliverable): for each of the (now 17) PDFs, walks pages in order; detects the 4 target tables by testing the top 35% of a page against fixed header strings and deriving column x-boundaries; sets a `seen_devcap` flag on entering dev_capital; applies a **STOP rule** — once `seen_devcap` is true, any subsequent page whose top text matches a STOP header (`capital expenditure`, `public account expenditure`, `schedule`, `object classification`, `demand-wise`, `demand budget estimates`, `statement of estimated`) halts extraction for that PDF, preventing Schedule‑I/III bleed. import io

p = r'C:\Users\Ali\desktop\projects\code\ra-ship\DOCUMENTATION_RECON.md'
s = io.open(p, encoding='utf-8').read()

new = u"""## 1. Corpus and location

### The registry

Two CSVs define the registered acquisition. Both hold **363 rows**, and both are replicated byte-identically across several paths \u2014 they are copies, not separate documents.

| Logical file | Purpose | Copies |
|---|---|---|
| `sources.csv` | URL and discovery plan; 11 columns | `Agent Files/RA_WORKSPACE/02_sources/pbs-corpus/sources.csv`; `Source Documents Organized/Provenance/Source Discovery Registry.csv`; `ABS_PES_PBS_Extraction_Test/01_source_documents/PBS/pbs-corpus-sources.csv` |
| `manifest.csv` | Fetched-file record with hashes; 18 columns | `Agent Files/RA_WORKSPACE/02_sources/pbs-corpus/manifest.csv`; `Source Documents Organized/Provenance/Source Registry - URLs and File Metadata.csv` |

Companion evidence: `fetch_log.jsonl` (727 lines, append-only, one entry per attempt), `reports/gap_report.md`, `reproducibility.md`, and `harvest_evidence/` holding an index plus two manual-harvest JSON files for Punjab and Sindh.

**Field completeness in `manifest.csv`, out of 363 rows.** Acquisition metadata is complete; document-characterization fields are entirely empty.

| Field group | Filled | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `jurisdiction`, `doc_type`, `fiscal_year`, `filename`, `sha256`, `bytes`, `source_url`, `harvest_method`, `http_status`, `downloaded_at` | 363 / 363 | Complete |
| `notes` | 355 / 363 | All 355 carry the literal value `page_count_error:TypeError` |
| `last_modified` | 352 / 363 | |
| `volume` | 342 / 363 | |
| `etag` | 175 / 363 | |
| `page_count`, `is_born_digital`, `scanned_page_pct`, `language_flag` | **0 / 363** | The classification pass (`scripts/classify.py`) was stopped as too slow |

The consequence: every registered file traces to an official URL and verifies by hash, but **nothing in the corpus is classified as born-digital or scanned, and no page counts exist.** Extraction planning gets no input from the registry.

### Coverage by jurisdiction

Registered file counts. Federal is the only jurisdiction holding PES; FB appears only for Federal and Gilgit-Baltistan.

| Jurisdiction | ABS | DFG | WP | PES | FB | Files | FY span |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Federal | 10 | 58 | 10 | 76 | 3 | 157 | 2017-18 \u2192 2026-27 |
| Khyber Pakhtunkhwa | 10 | 125 | 36 | \u2014 | \u2014 | 171 | 2017-18 \u2192 2026-27 |
| Gilgit-Baltistan | 8 | \u2014 | \u2014 | \u2014 | 5 | 13 | 2019-20 \u2192 2026-27 |
| Sindh | 9 | \u2014 | 2 | \u2014 | \u2014 | 11 | 2018-19 \u2192 2026-27 |
| Punjab | \u2014 | \u2014 | 7 | \u2014 | \u2014 | 7 | 2017-18 \u2192 2024-25 |
| Balochistan | 2 | \u2014 | 2 | \u2014 | \u2014 | 4 | 2025-26 \u2192 2026-27 |

Against the 40 or 50 fiscal-year \u00d7 document-family cells each jurisdiction could hold, `reports/gap_report.md` records 134 absent cells:

| Jurisdiction | Cells expected | Fetched | Coverage |
|---|---|---|---|
| Federal | 50 | 42 | 84.0% |
| Khyber Pakhtunkhwa | 40 | 30 | 75.0% |
| Gilgit-Baltistan | 40 | 12 | 30.0% |
| Sindh | 40 | 11 | 27.5% |
| Punjab | 40 | 7 | 17.5% |
| Balochistan | 40 | 4 | 10.0% |

**What is missing, by jurisdiction:**

- **Federal** \u2014 ABS, DFG and WP complete for all ten years. PES complete 2017-18 to 2025-26, missing 2026-27. FB held only for 2024-25 onward; missing 2017-18 through 2023-24.
- **Khyber Pakhtunkhwa** \u2014 the only jurisdiction with complete coverage on three families: ABS, DFG and WP present every year 2017-18 to 2026-27. FB missing for all ten years.
- **Gilgit-Baltistan** \u2014 ABS missing 2017-18, 2018-19 and 2020-21. FB present 2021-22 to 2025-26. DFG and WP missing entirely.
- **Sindh** \u2014 ABS complete except 2017-18. WP held only for 2025-26 and 2026-27. DFG and FB missing entirely.
- **Punjab** \u2014 WP only, and only 2017-18 through 2022-23 plus 2024-25. ABS, DFG and FB missing for all ten years.
- **Balochistan** \u2014 ABS and WP for 2025-26 and 2026-27 only. Everything else missing, a 90% gap.

Punjab and Sindh had to be harvested manually because their robots policies prohibit automated listing-page scraping, which is the direct cause of their two lowest-coverage positions.

### Physical files against the registry

| Location | Files | Size | Relationship to registry |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Agent Files/RA_WORKSPACE/02_sources/pbs-corpus/raw/` | 363 | 1,993,367,302 bytes | **Exact 1:1 match.** federal 157, KP 171, GB 13, Sindh 11, Balochistan 4, Punjab 7 |
| `Source Documents Organized/` | 933 | 3.20 GiB | 363 registered + 568 unregistered + 2 provenance CSVs |
|   \u21b3 `Federal/` | 723 | | 157 in `Reproducible Federal Source Corpus/` (exact replica of the registry's federal set) plus **566 legacy files with no registry record** |
|   \u21b3 `Provincial/` | 206 | | Exactly matches the registry's provincial counts |
|   \u21b3 `Provenance/` | 2 | | The two registry CSVs |

**568 of the 933 physical files in the canonical tree have no provenance record.** All 568 are federal, in legacy sub-collections: Pakistan Economic Surveys FY2015-16 to FY2024-25 (291), Federal Budget Documents FY2015-16 to FY2025-26 (130), PES Archive Copy FY2021-22 to FY2025-26 (118), Annual Budget Statements FY2010-11 to FY2026-27 (17), Budget in Brief FY2021-22 to FY2026-27 (6), FBR Year Books FY2022-23 to FY2024-25 (4). No provincial file is unregistered.

One detail worth recording: those legacy per-year folders hold 11 fewer files than their source in `Budget EDA/`. The difference is the per-edition `manifest.csv`, dropped from each of the 11 edition folders during the copy. The URLs those manifests carried survive only in the `Budget EDA/` original.

### Integrity and duplication

**Within the registered 363: zero SHA-256 collisions.** Every registered file is byte-unique; multi-volume DFG archives with differing hashes are genuinely distinct documents. A structural audit recorded 900 PDFs and 29 ZIPs passing integrity checks, with no confirmed corrupt file.

**Across the whole repository the picture differs sharply.** A SHA-256 comparison found **393 duplicate-content groups across 1,278 files \u2014 885 excess copies.** 385 of those groups straddle `Source Documents Organized/` and `02_Source_Documents_Read_Only/`. PES historical supplements for FY2017-18 through FY2020-21 each appear roughly 30 times. This figure exists only as prose; no machine-readable deduplication report backs it.

One upstream error is already isolated. `Source Documents Organized/Federal/Pakistan Economic Surveys FY2015-16 to FY2024-25/Repeated Historical Statistical Supplements/` holds 9 files named for 9 different fiscal years that are all byte-identical, SHA-256 `29b2ee8b\u2026f23`. The FY2018-19 Statistical Supplement was published or downloaded under nine years' filenames. Segregating them prevents nine wrong-year attributions.

A second correction is recorded in the canonical README: 26 KP Citizen Budget PDFs were moved out of `White Papers/` into a new `Citizen Budgets/` folder, leaving `White Papers/` with exactly 10, one per fiscal year. In `manifest.csv` both remain typed `doc_type=WP`, which is why KP's WP count reads high at 36.

### The replica trees

| Collection | Files | Size | Status | Provenance carried |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Agent Files/RA_WORKSPACE/02_sources/pbs-corpus/raw/` | 363 | 1.99 GB | **Canonical acquisition** | Full registry: URL, SHA-256, HTTP metadata |
| `Source Documents Organized/` | 933 | 3.20 GiB | **Canonical presentation** | Two provenance CSVs, covering 363 of 933 |
| `02_Source_Documents_Read_Only/` | 651 | 1.35 GiB | Replica, explicitly non-canonical | Partial \u2014 `manifest.csv` retained for federal budget documents and PES; **none** for ABS 2010-2026 or FBR year books |
| `Budget EDA/Budget EDA/data/` | 452 | 1.8 GB | Inherited original | 21 per-year `manifest.csv` files, columns `label,file_name,url` |
| `Arsalan Archive/Archive/` | 492 | 2.3 GB | Inherited, mixed | 4 manifests under PES only; raw ABS PDFs carry **no URL record**; also holds `__MACOSX` and venv debris |

Treat `Source Documents Organized/` as canonical for presentation and `pbs-corpus/raw/` as canonical for acquisition. The other three are replicas or handover libraries and must not be counted as additional documents.

### What the corpus does not contain

Searched by filename across every tree, excluding library-code false positives such as `huggingface_hub/lfs.py`:

- **No Labour Force Survey (LFS).** No PSLM, no HIES, no MICS, no Census report.
- **No HDI or UNDP material of any kind.** Zero matches repository-wide.
- **No Pakistan Bureau of Statistics survey publication.** The `PBS` in `ABS_PES_PBS_Extraction_Test/` refers to the fiscal-document registry, not Bureau of Statistics content. `01_source_documents/PBS/` holds only the registry CSV, a README, and a `SOURCE_SELECTION.md` stating that no PBS survey PDF was found and one must still be chosen.

Labour-force, poverty and social-protection figures **do** exist, but only as chapters reprinted inside the Pakistan Economic Survey, which is a Finance Division publication rather than a Bureau of Statistics survey:

- `Agent Files/RA_WORKSPACE/02_sources/pbs-corpus/raw/federal/{2019-20,2020-21,2024-25}/PES_population_labor_force_and_employment.pdf`
- `.../raw/federal/{2019-20,2020-21,2024-25}/PES_social_protection.pdf`
- `02_Source_Documents_Read_Only/Federal_Government/Pakistan_Economic_Survey_2015_to_2025/2019-20/Population_Labour_Force_And_Employment.pdf`
- Poverty annexures at `.../2015-16/Annexure_Iii_Poverty.pdf` and `.../2017-18/Annex_Iii_Poverty.pdf`; `Social_Protection.pdf` across 2018-19, 2019-20, 2020-21, 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25

The 22 `Statistical_Supplement` archives were checked for survey content and hold none \u2014 the FY2024-25 archive, for instance, contains a single 7.37 MB `supplement_2024-25.pdf`.

### Derived datasets

One structured dataset exists, at `Arsalan Archive/Archive/ABS Dataset/files/`, derived from the 17-edition federal ABS series FY2010-11 to FY2025-26:

| File | Shape | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `subcodes_long.csv` | 13,248 rows \u00d7 16 cols | `function_code, parent_function_code, hierarchy_level, function_name, classification_system, appears_in_account_types, first_year_in_data, last_year_in_data, abs_edition_fy, refers_to_fy, expenditure_nature, account_type, estimate_type, value_PKR_mn, unit, source_pdf_url` |
| `subcodes_wide_enriched.csv` | 69 rows \u00d7 202 cols | 9 metadata columns plus 192 value columns keyed `{fy}_{nature}_{account_type}_{estimate}_PKR_mn` |

Traceability stops at `source_pdf_url`. There is no page, table or cell-level provenance, a limitation `TEST2_PROTOCOL_AND_SOP.md` also records.

"""

start = s.index(u'## 1. Corpus and location')
end = s.index(u'## 2. Regular updates and crawlers')
s = s[:start] + new + s[end:]
io.open(p, 'w', encoding='utf-8', newline='').write(s)
print('rewrote section 1; now %d lines' % s.count('\n'))
